snaps.render:
[K1001] CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.
[K1002] Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2.
[K1003] SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.
[K1004] LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs ≥3× smaller Δ it wins only 22/36 corpus pairs, BUT 6/6 when its MLP is better (more LN+residual; q_65db92), 12/22 at equal arch, 4/8 when worse; prefer Adam 3e-3 (loses 2/35) over RMSprop at equal lr. (b) Bigram LMs: Δ optimum 0.1-0.3, d128 post-LN transformer 0.03-0.1 (K1071). (c) MLP classification: lr 3e-3 is safe on XOR/spiral, NOT on 1024-row tabular (optimum Δ shrinks with epochs, K1073). (d) UNIVARIATE regression, multi-layer net width≥64: Adam-family lr·T≥1 overshoots (K1072).
[K1005] Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. EXCEPTION — tasks whose CE can reach ~1e-4 (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr≥1e-3): torch Adam with coupled weight_decay≥1e-3 loses to an AdamW or wd=0 twin by 30-500× (K1040, q_6a81f1); β2 there flips with lr, so do not use β2 to explain it.
[K1006] MLP ARCHITECTURE DEFAULT (same optimizer for all choices; regression, XOR, spiral, tabular when Δ<0.1): score = (#LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual, MINUS 1 if a NON-residual depth≥4 net's LAST block has no LN (K1061); pick the highest. Ties: on regression ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, then later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Corpus MLP arch-only hits 74/110 (spiral 12/16, tabular 17/32). More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 multivariate, 57-12 univariate, 41-4 tabular Δ<0.1. Overrides: regression deep vs shallow (K1074); spiral residual ≥2 blocks deeper (K1020); shared-SGD regression rectifier vs SiLU (K1039); XOR ≥8 feat. Δ≥0.05 (K1018, K1065); tabular Δ≥0.1 (K1009/K1073).
[K1008] MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).
[K1009] Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive / piecewise / sparse_interaction rules): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (Δ from the core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad), the boundary is already learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower wins 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). This 2-regime rule picks 26/32 tabular arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.
[K1012] When Δs are close (mixed questions, rankings): a ≥4× Δ gap beats architecture (higher Δ wins 35/40 even vs a net with 2+ more LN/residual). Within ~3×, a clearly better MLP (≥2 more LN blocks/residual) wins 11/19 — treat as a toss-up leaning architecture. Δ also saturates: once both Δ≳0.3, extra Δ wins only ~62% (then use lr-ceiling, tabular-overfit and architecture rules). Rankings: sort by log Δ, then architecture; near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2 / ln V, MSE≈Var(y)) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture, not small lr differences.
[K1015] Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).
[K1017] Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model, layer count: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 FEWER layers wins 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11; 0.02≤Δ<0.1 COIN FLIP (fewer 8/15; q_4f69f2, q_9344eb: 2-layer beat 1-layer) - do not decide by depth there; Δ<0.02 deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE - wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 smaller wins 5/6, order by d_model ascending then layers (q_17f213; K1068). GRU vs transformer: K1075; lr: K1071.
[K1018] XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 noise distractors), same optimizer: the architecture rule FLIPS at shared core-rule Δ≈0.05. Δ≥0.05 (e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU (lab 15/16, CE ratio 0.78; corpus 6/6); FEWER LayerNorms win (more-LN wins only 8/32 lab, 5/11 corpus); a ≤2-block net beats one ≥3 blocks deeper (lab 5/5, ratio 0.51; corpus 2/3; q_bfba99, q_e914b6). Δ<0.05 (e.g. SGD m0.9 3e-4×1024): normal rule - more LN wins 33/41 (ratio 0.93), deeper beats shallow (shallow 4/14), activation ~coin flip (smooth 3/8). With <8 features keep deeper (7/7); more-LN there is a coin flip at Δ≥0.05 (4/8). Depth×residual: K1065.
[K1019] SGD gradient-scale calibration for the Δ rule (K1001 assumes raw |g|≈0.01), fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs. Bigram LM: use |g|≈0.003 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/30, plain ≈ lr/300): larger-Δ correct 68/70 vs 63/70 at 0.01; SGD m=0.9 beat Adam/AdamW/RMSprop in only 1/18 LM pairs (1/4 even at nominal Δ parity). MSE regression with momentum 0.9: use |g|≈0.03 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/3): 59/71 vs 54/71; it wins 11/19 when the adaptive Δ is ≤4× its 0.01-estimate. Classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression: keep 0.01. Plain SGD wins only 3/141 pairs when the adaptive Δ is >15× larger. These calibrations assume the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less credit (K1038).
[K1020] TWO-SPIRAL classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual as tie-break - UNLESS the residual net is ≥2 blocks DEEPER. Same residual status: more LN wins (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-more-LN vs residual-fewer-LN at 0.03≤Δ<0.5: plain wins when depths are within ±1 (lab 58/66, ratio 0.85; q_31abed), but a residual net ≥2 blocks deeper wins (lab 6/8, ratio 0.71; q_40922b: depth-5 residual, Adagrad 3e-3×1024, beat depth-3 plain nets with more LN; K1066). Δ<0.03: coin flip (residual 14/24). Δ≥0.5: residual 5/6. Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain ≥1-LN nets at Δ<0.5 (lab 8/59), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13).
[K1022] LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.
[K1033] Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
[K1038] SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1019 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).
[K1039] SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).
[K1040] Spiral coupled weight decay (two-spiral CE, 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr 1e-3-3e-3, T≈1024, CE can reach ~1e-4): torch Adam with weight_decay≥1e-3 (L2 coupled into the adaptive gradient) is far worse than AdamW at the same wd or any wd=0 twin: controlled plain ReLU d2 w48 lr 3e-3: Adam wd1e-3 CE 0.003, wd1e-2 0.044 vs AdamW wd1e-3/1e-2 ≤2e-4, wd=0 3e-5-1.8e-4 (AdamW beats Adam 12/12 cells, ratio 0.002-0.03); q_6a81f1 AdamW beat Adam (both wd1e-3) on 1-layer GELU w256. Rank coupled-Adam+wd below such twins regardless of β2. β2 alone flips with lr (0.95 better at lr≥1e-3 plain nets, 0.999 at 3e-4): weak tie-break. Not seen on bigram LM (q_e6d625).
[K1056] TABULAR classification (synthetic, 1024 rows), once trained (shared core-rule Δ≥0.1, same optimizer/lr/T): prefer GELU/SiLU over ReLU/LeakyReLU. Smooth wins 23/25 lab within-set pairs (~11 sets, median test-CE ratio ~0.80; smooth_additive 14/14, sparse_interaction 5/6, piecewise 4/5); corpus 16/16 (K1009). At Δ 0.01-0.1 only a tendency (44/74, ratio 0.87); at Δ<0.01 no effect (8/19, ratio 1.00) - decide by LN/depth instead. Activation-only matched pairs 19/28. q_b68ab2: plain SiLU RMSprop 1e-4×2048 (Δ0.2) beat residual LeakyReLU nets at larger Δ.
[K1057] UNIVARIATE regression, same MLP, Adam/AdamW vs RMSprop: Adam-family wins at almost any lr pairing - lab 78/88 same-arch within-set pairs (median MSE ratio ~0.06): equal lr 21/24; Adam at 3-33× LOWER lr 21/23; Adam at 3-10×+ higher lr 36/41. Adam lr≤RMSprop lr subset: non-oscillatory targets 15/15 (ratio 0.02), sin/cos(2πx) targets 27/32 (0.18). Corpus 4/5 (only loss: Adam 3e-5 vs RMSprop 3e-3, 100× gap). Do not credit RMSprop's early-step amplification (q_7f8fb0: AdamW 3e-5 beat RMSprop 3e-5 and 1e-4). Wide-net lr·T≥1 overshoot (K1055) still applies first. NOT multivariate (lab 10/18, ratio 0.97; corpus 5/9).
[K1059] Classification MLPs (tabular, XOR, spiral), NON-residual, depth≥2, all choices on the same SGD (plain or momentum): the net whose LAST hidden block has LayerNorm wins 31/31 lab within-set pairs (14 sets, median CE ratio 0.69) - even when it has FEWER LayerNorms in total (11/11, ratio 0.76). An unnormalized tail undoes earlier LN (q_1af0fa: a deep net with internal LN but 2 unnormalized final blocks lost to a shallower wider net; normalizing those blocks cut CE 0.69→0.47 in a controlled rerun). With adaptive optimizers the edge is weaker: Adam 70/102 (ratio 0.92), Adagrad 21/35 (~0.99). Regression: univariate 17/25, multivariate 20/35 - not reliable.
[K1061] CLASSIFICATION MLPs (XOR/spiral/tabular), shared optimizer, Δ<0.1: RESIDUAL net vs NON-residual depth≥4 net with MORE LayerNorms — look at the plain net's LAST hidden block. Last block un-normalized → the residual net wins (lab SGD 16/16, CE ratio 0.72; adaptive 5/9; corpus 5/5): LNs followed by an unnormalized tail don't count. Last block LN'd → family-dependent: XOR+SGD plain wins 9/10; spiral+Adam-family plain wins 22/23 (residual CE ×1.3-1.4); spiral+SGD residual wins (lab 3/3, controlled 2/2, ratio 0.3-0.8); tabular ~coin flip (lab 12/27, corpus 6/6 plain). Moving LN to the last block (same count) lowered plain CE in 6/6 controlled cells.
[K1063] UNIVARIATE regression, RMSprop vs RMSprop (same MLP, different lr): the LOWER RMSprop lr usually wins, even at small Δ — lab larger-lr wins 9/42 (10 experiment groups; T=256 width≥128: 3/24, median MSE ratio 3.6; lr 1e-4 vs 3e-5: 3/11), corpus 2/3. At T=1024 on narrow nets it is a coin flip (4/9). RMSprop as the larger-Δ choice against Adam/AdamW of the same net also loses (lab 0/21 at RMSprop lr≥3e-4). Do not apply max-Δ to RMSprop on univariate MSE; multivariate is a coin flip (11/25).
[K1065] XOR with ≥8 input features, once trained (shared optimizer, Δ≥0.05): depth helps only WITH residuals. A deeper NON-residual MLP loses to a shallower one even at a 1-2 block gap (lab deeper wins 1/31, 13 sets, CE ×1.23); a deeper RESIDUAL MLP beats a shallower one at a 1-2 block gap (8/13, 7 sets, CE ×0.82) but loses at gap ≥3 (lab 0/4, corpus 2-vs-5 block 2/3 shallow, K1018). q_164857 (AdamW 1e-4×2048): 3-block residual SiLU nets beat 1-block w192 nets, and the 3-block non-residual GELU net was last. At Δ<0.05 depth is a coin flip (plain 10/25, residual 14/19 deeper wins).
[K1066] TWO-SPIRAL classification, DEEP vs SHALLOW (same optimizer): a deeper (≥3 block) RESIDUAL MLP with MORE LayerNorms than a shallow (≤2 block) net wins almost always — lab 51/55 (adaptive Δ≥0.05 34/35, CE ratio 0.38; adaptive Δ<0.05 11/14; SGD 6/6, ratio 0.36), corpus 8/8 (ratio 0.76) — even if the shallow net is much wider. Deeper NON-residual nets are unreliable: lab 30/32 with more LN but corpus 0/7 (q_5fe255, q_774f6c had unnormalized last blocks) — credit them only if their last block is LN'd (K1061). Deeper residual with ≤ the shallow net's LN: lab 33/43, corpus 0/2 — tendency only. q_d7ea11: 3-LN residual deep net beat the shallow wide pick.
[K1068] BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER d_model × Δ (same optimizer/lr/T, different d_model): wider wins only while under-trained; the flip is at Δ≈0.1. Δ 0.02-0.1: LARGER d_model wins (lab 21/23, corpus 13/13, CE ratio ~0.98). Δ 0.1-0.5 (e.g. Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024): SMALLER d_model wins (lab 26/27 — d64 beat d128 20/21, d32 beat d128 2/2 with ratio 1.14; corpus 7/11, d64 vs d128 3/3). Δ≥0.5: smaller wins (lab 10/12, corpus 5/6). Δ<0.02: coin flip, SGD favors wider. Fills K1017's gap. q_02539d: d128 AdamW 3e-4×512 (Δ0.15) lost to d64 RMSprop 3e-3×512.
[K1069] BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER head count (same d_model/layers/optimizer/T): fewer heads (2 vs 4) wins 12/15 lab pairs. At Δ<0.5 it is only a tie-break (CE ratio ≈1.00); at Δ≥0.5 it matters (lab 4/4, ratio 1.01-1.07; controlled q_d6dddb d128 AdamW 3e-3×256: 2 heads −0.18 nats vs 4 heads, d_ff 128→256 only +0.07) and head count outranks a 2× d_ff difference (fewer heads + larger d_ff beat more heads + smaller d_ff 4/4). q_d6dddb gold: 2-head d_ff256 beat 4-head d_ff128. Order: d_model/layers (K1017) first, then heads, then d_ff.
[K1070] CLASSIFICATION MLPs (spiral/XOR/tabular), RMSprop vs Adam/AdamW at the SAME lr, same net, T≤1024: RMSprop usually WINS — lab 17/20 matched pairs (median Adam/RMS CE ratio 1.12; XOR 1.31, tabular 1.20, spiral 1.12), controlled 7/8; epoch q_4c1af8, q_e4c256 (XOR 3e-4, 3e-5), q_ebfdb8 (tabular 1e-4). Treat RMSprop ≈ Adam at ~1.5× lr (Adam at 3.3× lr wins 5/9). Edge shrinks with T (tabular ratio 1.19 at T=256 → 1.04 at 1024; T=2048 Adam 1/1) and vanishes once CE≈0. At lr≤3e-4 also on multivariate regression (4/4) and bigram LM (4/4). At lr≥1e-3 Adam wins: bigram transformer 5/5 (ratio 1.02-1.08; q_a97a96 RMSprop 3e-3 last), multivariate 6/6; univariate regression always Adam (K1057).
[K1071] BIGRAM LM learning-rate sweet spot (same model; choices differ in optimizer/lr/T; Δ per K1001): past a model-specific optimum MORE Δ LOSES - the solver's most common LM miss. d32/d64 transformers and GRUs: optimum Δ≈0.1-0.3 (Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024, 1e-3 at T=256; Adagrad 3e-3); ≥2× more Δ than a rival already at 0.1-0.3 loses (lab transformer 1/44, GRU 1/6, CE +2-20%); Δ≥1 loses to any rival with Δ≥0.03 (lab 0/17; q_c3a179). d_model=128 post-LN transformer: optimum ≈0.03-0.1; larger loses 0/11 once rival Δ≥0.03 (q_88802d AdamW 3e-3×256 last). Below the optimum max-Δ holds (13/13; GRU 14/15). Corpus: pick 'Δ nearest 0.2 (0.1 for d128)' 52/65 vs max-Δ 43/65.
[K1072] UNIVARIATE regression lr OVERSHOOT (same multi-layer MLP, depth≥2, width≥64; choices differ in optimizer/lr): Adam/AdamW/RMSprop Δ=lr·T≥1 loses to a Δ≈0.1-0.5 rival (Adam/AdamW 1e-4×1024, 3e-4×512, Adagrad 3e-3): corpus 5/5; lab larger-Δ wins w64 0/12 (MSE ×8.8), w128 5/18 (×5.5), w256 1/13 (×4.4); controlled 11/12. A rival with Δ<0.05 is still undertrained and wins only if the high side has Δ≥5 (q_f609cc: Adam 3e-3 beat Adam 3e-5; lab 3/7). Larger Δ still wins at width≤32 (lab 9/16; q_cdbed5 w16), on depth-1 nets (lab 8/8, corpus 10/10) and on MULTIVARIATE regression (corpus 4/5, lab 10/10).
[K1073] TABULAR classification Δ sweet spot vs EPOCHS (synthetic, 1024 rows; E=total_samples_seen/1024; core-rule Δ). Below Δ≈0.03 more Δ wins at E=4 (lab 56/56). The CE-optimal Δ then SHRINKS with E on smooth_additive: E=4 ≈0.25 (Δ0.77 lost to 0.26, 3/3 controlled); E=16 ≈0.08 (controlled 2/2; q_c1581a RMSprop 1e-4×256 bs64 Δ0.026 beat Adam 1e-3 Δ0.26 and AdamW 3e-3 Δ0.77); E=32 ≈0.05-0.15: Δ≥0.5 loses (lab 24/28) and ≥3× more loses 1/15 once small Δ≥0.03. sparse_interaction: optimum ≈0.25 at E 4-16, 0.15 at E 32; larger loses once small Δ≥0.1 (lab 5/33, CE ×1.44). piecewise tolerates more (larger wins 10/10 at E=16). Then use architecture (K1009/K1033).
[K1074] REGRESSION DEPTH (univariate/multivariate MSE MLPs; picking the shallow-wide net is the most common univariate miss): a depth≥4 net with ≥1 LayerNorm (and ≥ the rival's LN count) beats a depth≤2 net - even a wider and/or residual one - whenever its core-rule Δ is ≥1/3 of the shallow net's: univariate corpus 31/38, lab 380/461 (MSE ratio ~0.15-0.2); multivariate corpus 18/22, lab 323/435 (~0.7). If deep Δ <1/3 of shallow Δ the shallow net wins (uni corpus 8/9, lab 228/295; multi 6/6, 159/215). Deeper residual beats shallower non-residual 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide 70-32. Deep NON-residual 0-LN stacks attenuate signal and usually lose.
[K1075] BIGRAM LM GRU vs post-LN transformer (same optimizer/lr/T): decide by the shared core-rule Δ band. Δ<0.02 (nearly frozen: Adam-family ≤3e-5 at T≤512, SGD ≤3e-3): GRU wins, even vs larger d_model when alpha≤1 (corpus 8/8, controlled GRU 5/6; q_5e328e GRU64×2 beat d128). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: a transformer of EQUAL or LARGER d_model wins (lab GRU 1/20; controlled 2-layer GRU 0/9 at every T 256-2048; q_9344eb GRU64×2 last at AdamW 3e-5×2048, even below d32×3 d_ff256); GRU64 vs d32: GRU 9/9 observational, lean GRU only if 1-layer. 0.1≤Δ<0.5: GRU wins 8/9 (any d_model). Δ≥0.5: GRU 3/3 (transformer overshoots, K1071).

summary: 第 1–6 轮已有完整逐题记录；e7 已保存 22 题、尚未完成。最新 kb_0006 共 35 条，e6 只更新引用反馈。e5 宏观评测：val +1.04 ±1.82pt，旧 test +1.65 ±2.95pt，尚不能排除零增益。
texts: CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.

Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2.

SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs ≥3× smaller Δ it wins only 22/36 corpus pairs, BUT 6/6 when its MLP is better (more LN+residual; ratio 0.04, q_65db92), 12/22 at equal arch, 4/8 when worse. Adam 3e-3 loses only 2/35 overall: prefer it over RMSprop at equal lr. (b) Post-LN transformer LMs with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4 (worst d_model=128, T≥1024); GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification: lr 3e-3 is safe. (d) UNIVARIATE regression on a wide (≥128) multi-layer net: Adam-family lr·T≥0.5 overshoots (wide-net univariate ceiling rule).

Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. EXCEPTION — tasks whose CE can reach ~1e-4 (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr≥1e-3): torch Adam with coupled weight_decay≥1e-3 loses to an AdamW or wd=0 twin by 30-500× (K1040, q_6a81f1); β2 there flips with lr, so do not use β2 to explain it.

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then (tabular/multivariate) later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Picks 92/128 arch-only winners. More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression plain+more-LN beats residual+less-LN (13/17 multivar, 14/20 univar). Exceptions: shared-SGD regression: rectifier beats SiLU despite 1 fewer LN (K1039); SPIRAL: residual first only if Δ<0.03 or ≥0.5 (K1020); XOR ≥8 feat., Δ≥0.05: smooth act. (K1018); tabular Δ≥0.1: K1009/K1021.

Regression depth × residual (uni/multivariate MSE, any budget): a deeper residual MLP beats a shallower non-residual one 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide at similar params 70-32 (51-19 when lr·T<0.1); at equal depth extra width is a coin flip (5-5). Oscillatory/composite targets (sin(2πx)…, cos(2π sin…)) amplify the depth advantage: composition of 4-5 normalized residual blocks generates high-frequency curvature that 1-2 layer nets cannot reach within the budget. Non-residual deep stacks without LN are the exception: they attenuate signal and usually lose.

Activation × task: on MSE regression (univariate and multivariate) prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, EVEN for smooth targets (cubic/polynomial, sin/cos): do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Pairwise vs other activations (same optimizer): LeakyReLU wins 51/77, ReLU 42/67, GELU 30/64, SiLU only 29/96. SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so stacked blocks attenuate signal/gradient. Epoch-7 misses q_718eda and q_cfc265 picked SiLU for smoothness and lost to ReLU-family nets (both also confounded with LN placement). Flips for well-trained tabular classification (GELU/SiLU win 16/16; K1009) and XOR ≥8 features (K1018); weak on spiral.

Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive / piecewise / sparse_interaction rules): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (Δ from the core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad), the boundary is already learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower wins 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). This 2-regime rule picks 26/32 tabular arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.

XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss stays on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so (i) Δ is decisive — choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70 and are near-tied; (ii) among equal optimizers, deep RESIDUAL blocks with LN win: deeper+residual beats shallower plain 33-14 on classification, more-LN wins 20-5 on spiral (Δ≥0.01), deeper wins XOR at every budget (26-11). A 1-2 layer plain net rarely escapes the plateau in 256-512 steps. Spiral difficulty scales with turns: 1 turn best CE ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (nearly everything stuck → pick largest Δ).

Bigram LM GRU vs post-LN transformer (same optimizer/lr/T): the GRU edge depends on d_model. GRU d_model > transformer's (GRU 64 vs T 32): GRU wins 19/20 (corpus 9/9, lab 10/11; q_ce881e GRU64×1 1st). Transformer d_model larger (T128 vs GRU 32/64): transformer wins 13/14 (lab). Equal d_model: toss-up (corpus GRU64×2 vs T64 9/10, lab 1/6; q_ce881e GRU32×2 beat only 1 of 3 d32 transformers) — lean GRU only at d_model 64. Within transformers use the bigram transformer shape rule (K1017).

When Δs are close (mixed questions, rankings): a ≥4× Δ gap beats architecture (higher Δ wins 35/40 even vs a net with 2+ more LN/residual). Within ~3×, a clearly better MLP (≥2 more LN blocks/residual) wins 11/19 — treat as a toss-up leaning architecture. Δ also saturates: once both Δ≳0.3, extra Δ wins only ~62% (then use lr-ceiling, tabular-overfit and architecture rules). Rankings: sort by log Δ, then architecture; near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2 / ln V, MSE≈Var(y)) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture, not small lr differences.

Bigram LM optimizer sweet spot: labels are sampled from P(y|x), so gradients carry irreducible noise and the achievable gain is only ~0.1-0.8 nats below ln V. Among choices with Δ≥0.1, prefer the one with Δ nearest ~0.3 (e.g. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop 3e-4 at T=512-1024, Adagrad 3e-3); treat Δ≥1 (lr≥1e-3 at T≥1024, lr 3e-3 at T≥512) as likely overshoot. Below Δ≈0.1 ordinary max-Δ still applies. This 'nearest 0.3' scoring picks 52/66 bigram optimizer/mixed winners vs 47/66 for plain max-Δ; adaptive-transformer winners are mostly lr 3e-4 (22/52). If all Δ<0.02 every LM stays ≈ln V and the GRU wins ties.

Dataset structure × depth (data-flip cue): the deeper-is-better preference (under Δ<0.1) is strong for smooth/compositional targets — tabular smooth_additive (deeper 24-8), XOR with ≤4 input features (15-4), oscillatory univariate targets — but weak or absent when the rule is piecewise_boundary (5-6) or sparse_interaction (6-3) or XOR has 8-16 distractor features (11-7); there prefer the most-LN candidate regardless of depth, EXCEPT XOR with ≥8 features at Δ≥0.05, where more-LN wins only 5/11 and GELU/SiLU decides (6/6; see XOR-distractor rule). Polynomial/low-frequency univariate targets reach MSE 1e-4-1e-5, so stability (Adam over RMSprop at high lr) decides.

Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.

Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model → fewer layers wins: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a), Δ≥0.5 8/11, 0.02≤Δ<0.1 8/15 (corpus 5/5, lab 3/10); Δ<0.02 all ≈ln V, deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE — wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger d_model wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512) smaller d_model wins 5/6 — wide post-LN overshoots (K1004b); order by d_model ascending, then layers (q_17f213). GRU vs transformer: K1011.

XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 pure-noise distractors) once trained (shared Δ≥0.05, e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): tabular-style reversal — GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU in 6/6 same-optimizer pairs, more-LN wins only 5/11, and SHALLOW-WIDE beats deep when the depth gap is ≥3 blocks (2-block vs 5-block: corpus 2/3, median CE ratio 0.64; q_bfba99 AdamW 3e-4×512: all three 2-block w192-256 nets beat both 5-block residual nets (3-4 LN), 2-LN SiLU first, 4-LN LeakyReLU last; controlled 4/4). q_e914b6: 2-layer SiLU w192 CE 0.11 beat 5-layer 3-LN 0.17. With ≤4 features keep deeper/more-LN (deeper 7/7); for Δ<0.05 the LN/depth rule holds for all XOR. Larger Δ still wins on XOR (6/7).

SGD gradient-scale calibration for the Δ rule (K1001 assumes raw |g|≈0.01), fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs. Bigram LM: use |g|≈0.003 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/30, plain ≈ lr/300): larger-Δ correct 68/70 vs 63/70 at 0.01; SGD m=0.9 beat Adam/AdamW/RMSprop in only 1/18 LM pairs (1/4 even at nominal Δ parity). MSE regression with momentum 0.9: use |g|≈0.03 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/3): 59/71 vs 54/71; it wins 11/19 when the adaptive Δ is ≤4× its 0.01-estimate. Classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression: keep 0.01. Plain SGD wins only 3/141 pairs when the adaptive Δ is >15× larger. These calibrations assume the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less credit (K1038).

Two-spiral classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual only as tie-break (K1006 sum). Same residual status: more LN wins at every Δ (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-with-more-LN vs residual-with-fewer-LN: 0.03≤Δ<0.5 plain wins 25/29 (lab 16/18, controlled 6/6 ratio 1.03-3.7; q_31abed, q_9c257e C>B; miss q_9c257e D>C); Δ<0.03 near coin flip (residual 14/24: corpus 5/5, lab 9/17, controlled 0/2); Δ≥0.5 mixed (residual lab 5/6, controlled 1/4 — only 2-turn at Δ1.5). Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain nets with ≥1 LN at Δ<0.5 (lab 8/59, CE ratio 1.07-1.27), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13). Equal LN: residual 13/16 at Δ<0.03, coin flip 0.03-0.1 (21/49).

Synthetic TABULAR classification Δ overshoot (lab, 10-seed, within-set, mostly T=256 = 4 epochs): once the smaller-Δ choice already has Δ≥0.1 (core-rule Δ; e.g. Adam 1e-3 at T=256, 1e-4 at T=1024), a ≥3× larger Δ LOSES on average: sparse_interaction larger-Δ wins 5/33 (median CE ratio 1.44), smooth_additive 22/55 (1.07), piecewise_boundary 36/58 (0.93); all tabular 63/146. For smaller Δ in 0.03-0.1 larger still wins 59-88%; below 0.03 ~95% at 4 epochs — but NOT at 32 epochs (32768 samples) on 16-D smooth_additive, where Δ 0.01-0.15 beats Δ≥0.5 (K1032). So target Δ≈0.1-0.3 and decide by architecture (K1009). E.g. q_86f129: GELU Adam 1e-4×1024 (Δ0.1) beat LeakyReLU AdamW 3e-3 (Δ3).

LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.

Tabular LONG-budget overfit (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 train rows, 8-16 features, total_samples_seen=32768 = 32 epochs): on smooth_additive the largest-Δ choice (Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3, Δ≥0.5) LOSES to Δ≈0.01-0.15 choices: lab 24/28 pairs (7 sets, median CE ratio 0.87); dataflip 4/4 (q_86f129; q_565490 Adam 3e-5 beat AdamW 1e-3, same net; q_e79cfd plain SGD 1e-3 + 2 LN beat Adam 1e-3; q_07b812 8-D: AdamW 3e-5×1024 beat AdamW 1e-3 and RMSprop 3e-3 on the same w192 net). Not at 4 epochs (T=256 bs16: Δ<0.03 loses 171/172). Piecewise/sparse_interaction at 32 epochs: mixed (larger Δ wins corpus 9/11 but lab 3/14) — decide by architecture (K1009/K1033).

Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).

SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1019 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).

SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).

Spiral coupled weight decay (two-spiral CE, 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr 1e-3-3e-3, T≈1024, CE can reach ~1e-4): torch Adam with weight_decay≥1e-3 (L2 coupled into the adaptive gradient) is far worse than AdamW at the same wd or any wd=0 twin: controlled plain ReLU d2 w48 lr 3e-3: Adam wd1e-3 CE 0.003, wd1e-2 0.044 vs AdamW wd1e-3/1e-2 ≤2e-4, wd=0 3e-5-1.8e-4 (AdamW beats Adam 12/12 cells, ratio 0.002-0.03); q_6a81f1 AdamW beat Adam (both wd1e-3) on 1-layer GELU w256. Rank coupled-Adam+wd below such twins regardless of β2. β2 alone flips with lr (0.95 better at lr≥1e-3 plain nets, 0.999 at 3e-4): weak tie-break. Not seen on bigram LM (q_e6d625).

UNIVARIATE regression, WIDE multi-layer MLP (width≥128, depth≥2), choices differ in optimizer/lr: lr·T≥1 OVERSHOOTS — prefer a choice with Δ≈0.1-0.5 (e.g. Adam/AdamW 1e-4×1024, 3e-4×512, Adagrad 3e-3) over Adam/AdamW/RMSprop at Δ≥1. Corpus optimizer-only 5/5 (q_3d7396 Adagrad 3e-3 beat AdamW 3e-3; q_9e733e; RMSprop lost 3/3); lab same-arch 8/9 (MSE ratio 3.4); controlled d2-4 w128-256 11/12 (13-1000×); q_2deb46. A rival with Δ<0.05 is still undertrained and loses (q_f609cc: Adam 3e-3 beat Adam 3e-5, d2 w256; lab 3/7) unless the high side has Δ≥5. NOT for 1-layer or narrow (≤96) nets (larger Δ wins corpus 10/10) nor multivariate regression (corpus 4/5, lab 10/10).

XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss stays on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so (i) Δ is decisive - choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70 and are near-tied; (ii) among equal optimizers, depth helps ONLY when it comes with RESIDUAL+LN: deeper+residual beats shallower plain 33-14, more-LN wins 20-5 on spiral (Δ≥0.01), deeper wins XOR 26-11. Do NOT credit extra depth in a NON-residual stack whose last blocks lack LN (q_f3d4a1: 2-block residual LN net beat 4-5-block plain stacks; see K1059). Spiral CE by turns: 1 turn ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 ~0.45-0.6, 3 ~0.52-0.69 (all stuck → pick largest Δ).

TABULAR classification (synthetic, 1024 rows), once trained (shared core-rule Δ≥0.1, same optimizer/lr/T): prefer GELU/SiLU over ReLU/LeakyReLU. Smooth wins 23/25 lab within-set pairs (~11 sets, median test-CE ratio ~0.80; smooth_additive 14/14, sparse_interaction 5/6, piecewise 4/5); corpus 16/16 (K1009). At Δ 0.01-0.1 only a tendency (44/74, ratio 0.87); at Δ<0.01 no effect (8/19, ratio 1.00) - decide by LN/depth instead. Activation-only matched pairs 19/28. q_b68ab2: plain SiLU RMSprop 1e-4×2048 (Δ0.2) beat residual LeakyReLU nets at larger Δ.

UNIVARIATE regression, same MLP, Adam/AdamW vs RMSprop: Adam-family wins at almost any lr pairing - lab 78/88 same-arch within-set pairs (median MSE ratio ~0.06): equal lr 21/24; Adam at 3-33× LOWER lr 21/23; Adam at 3-10×+ higher lr 36/41. Adam lr≤RMSprop lr subset: non-oscillatory targets 15/15 (ratio 0.02), sin/cos(2πx) targets 27/32 (0.18). Corpus 4/5 (only loss: Adam 3e-5 vs RMSprop 3e-3, 100× gap). Do not credit RMSprop's early-step amplification (q_7f8fb0: AdamW 3e-5 beat RMSprop 3e-5 and 1e-4). Wide-net lr·T≥1 overshoot (K1055) still applies first. NOT multivariate (lab 10/18, ratio 0.97; corpus 5/9).

Bigram LM, all choices nearly frozen (shared core-rule Δ<0.02, e.g. SGD lr≤3e-3 at T≤512, Adam-family lr≤3e-5 at T≤512) with alpha≤1: a 2-layer d64 GRU beats post-LN transformers EVEN of larger d_model (q_5e328e: GRU64×2 beat a d128×1 transformer, SGD Δ≈0.008). Corpus GRU64×2 vs transformer at matched optimizer: 8/8 at Δ<0.02 (4 qs, GRU lower CE by 0.04-0.14 nats), 18/19 at any Δ. K1011's 'larger-d_model transformer wins 13/14' was measured at alpha=1.4, Δ 0.02-0.1; at alpha 1.4 the transformer also won both Δ<0.02 lab pairs, so this exception needs low alpha.

Classification MLPs (tabular, XOR, spiral), NON-residual, depth≥2, all choices on the same SGD (plain or momentum): the net whose LAST hidden block has LayerNorm wins 31/31 lab within-set pairs (14 sets, median CE ratio 0.69) - even when it has FEWER LayerNorms in total (11/11, ratio 0.76). An unnormalized tail undoes earlier LN (q_1af0fa: a deep net with internal LN but 2 unnormalized final blocks lost to a shallower wider net; normalizing those blocks cut CE 0.69→0.47 in a controlled rerun). With adaptive optimizers the edge is weaker: Adam 70/102 (ratio 0.92), Adagrad 21/35 (~0.99). Regression: univariate 17/25, multivariate 20/35 - not reliable.

MLP ARCHITECTURE DEFAULT (same optimizer for all choices; regression, XOR, spiral, tabular when Δ<0.1): score = (#LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual, MINUS 1 if a NON-residual depth≥4 net's LAST block has no LN (K1061); pick the highest. Ties: on regression ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, then later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Corpus MLP arch-only hits 74/110 (71/110 without the tail penalty; spiral 12/16, tabular 17/32). More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 multivariate, 57-12 univariate, 41-4 tabular Δ<0.1. Exceptions: shared-SGD regression rectifier vs SiLU (K1039); spiral (K1020); XOR ≥8 feat. Δ≥0.05 (K1018, K1065); tabular Δ≥0.1 (K1009/K1021); regression deep vs shallow (K1060).

REGRESSION (univariate/multivariate MSE) DEEP vs SHALLOW-WIDE MLP: a depth≥4 net with ≥1 LayerNorm (and ≥ the rival's LN count) beats a depth≤2 net — even a wider and/or residual one — whenever its core-rule Δ is ≥1/3 of the shallow net's Δ. Univariate: corpus 31/38, lab 380/461 (82%), median MSE ratio ~0.15-0.2 (vs shallow residual: deep residual 84/93, deep plain 64/90 ratio 0.6). Multivariate: corpus 18/22, lab 323/435 (74%), ratio ~0.7. If the deep net's Δ is <1/3 of the shallow's, the shallow net wins (univariate corpus 8/9, lab 228/295; multivariate corpus 6/6, lab 159/215). Picking the shallow wide residual net is the most common univariate miss.

CLASSIFICATION MLPs (XOR/spiral/tabular), shared optimizer, Δ<0.1: RESIDUAL net vs NON-residual depth≥4 net with MORE LayerNorms — look at the plain net's LAST hidden block. Last block un-normalized → the residual net wins (lab SGD 16/16, CE ratio 0.72; adaptive 5/9; corpus 5/5): LNs followed by an unnormalized tail don't count. Last block LN'd → family-dependent: XOR+SGD plain wins 9/10; spiral+Adam-family plain wins 22/23 (residual CE ×1.3-1.4); spiral+SGD residual wins (lab 3/3, controlled 2/2, ratio 0.3-0.8); tabular ~coin flip (lab 12/27, corpus 6/6 plain). Moving LN to the last block (same count) lowered plain CE in 6/6 controlled cells.

BIGRAM LM TRANSFORMER learning-rate overshoot: an Adam/AdamW/RMSprop choice with Δ=lr·T≥1 (lr 3e-3 at T≥512, lr 1e-3 at T≥1024) LOSES to any rival with Δ≥0.03 — including SGD momentum 0.9 at lr≥1e-3 and Adagrad 3e-4 — lab 0/17 (3 sets, CE +2-18%), corpus 3/8. q_c3a179 (d32 1-layer, T=512): SGD m0.9 lr 3e-3 beat RMSprop 3e-3 and Adagrad 3e-4. Same model, Δ 0.3-1 also loses to Δ 0.1-0.3 (lab transformer 0/15, GRU 1/6). When every Δ<0.3, max-Δ still holds (lab GRU 50/50, transformer 21/27). So on bigram LMs never rank a high-lr adaptive choice first just for speed.

UNIVARIATE regression, RMSprop vs RMSprop (same MLP, different lr): the LOWER RMSprop lr usually wins, even at small Δ — lab larger-lr wins 9/42 (10 experiment groups; T=256 width≥128: 3/24, median MSE ratio 3.6; lr 1e-4 vs 3e-5: 3/11), corpus 2/3. At T=1024 on narrow nets it is a coin flip (4/9). RMSprop as the larger-Δ choice against Adam/AdamW of the same net also loses (lab 0/21 at RMSprop lr≥3e-4). Do not apply max-Δ to RMSprop on univariate MSE; multivariate is a coin flip (11/25).

UNIVARIATE regression lr overshoot width boundary (refines K1055): the Adam/AdamW Δ=lr·T≥1 overshoot on multi-layer (depth≥2) MLPs already appears at WIDTH 64, not only ≥128: same-net Adam Δ≥1 vs Adam Δ 0.03-1 — larger wins w64 0/12 (3 sets, MSE ×8.8), w128 5/18 (×5.5), w256 1/13 (×4.4); but at width ≤32 larger Δ still wins or ties (lab w32 9/16, corpus q_cdbed5 w16: AdamW 3e-3×1024 beat RMSprop 1e-4/3e-4). Depth-1 nets: larger Δ wins (lab 8/8 narrow).

XOR with ≥8 input features, once trained (shared optimizer, Δ≥0.05): depth helps only WITH residuals. A deeper NON-residual MLP loses to a shallower one even at a 1-2 block gap (lab deeper wins 1/31, 13 sets, CE ×1.23); a deeper RESIDUAL MLP beats a shallower one at a 1-2 block gap (8/13, 7 sets, CE ×0.82) but loses at gap ≥3 (lab 0/4, corpus 2-vs-5 block 2/3 shallow, K1018). q_164857 (AdamW 1e-4×2048): 3-block residual SiLU nets beat 1-block w192 nets, and the 3-block non-residual GELU net was last. At Δ<0.05 depth is a coin flip (plain 10/25, residual 14/19 deeper wins).

TWO-SPIRAL classification, DEEP vs SHALLOW (same optimizer): a deeper (≥3 block) RESIDUAL MLP with MORE LayerNorms than a shallow (≤2 block) net wins almost always — lab 51/55 (adaptive Δ≥0.05 34/35, CE ratio 0.38; adaptive Δ<0.05 11/14; SGD 6/6, ratio 0.36), corpus 8/8 (ratio 0.76) — even if the shallow net is much wider. Deeper NON-residual nets are unreliable: lab 30/32 with more LN but corpus 0/7 (q_5fe255, q_774f6c had unnormalized last blocks) — credit them only if their last block is LN'd (K1061). Deeper residual with ≤ the shallow net's LN: lab 33/43, corpus 0/2 — tendency only. q_d7ea11: 3-LN residual deep net beat the shallow wide pick.

MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).

BIGRAM LM GRU learning rate (same GRU net, choices differ in optimizer/lr; Δ per K1001): the best Δ is 0.1-0.5 (Adam/AdamW/RMSprop 3e-4 at T=512-1024, 1e-3 at T=256). Up to Δ≈0.5 larger Δ wins (lab 81/83 pairs, CE 1-8% lower). Above it, a Δ≥0.5 choice LOSES to a same-GRU rival with Δ 0.1-0.5: lab 7/8, corpus 3/3 (q_b704b4, q_f1b323), epoch q_326760 (RMSprop 1e-3×512 beat AdamW 3e-3×512) — margins only 0.5-1% CE. A Δ 0.5-1 choice still beats rivals with Δ<0.1 (lab 25/27, corpus 5/5; miss q_ae5159: Adam 3e-4×256 beat RMSprop 3e-3×256). SGD m=0 and Adagrad ≤3e-4 are Δ<0.1 here.

BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER d_model × Δ (same optimizer/lr/T, different d_model): wider wins only while under-trained; the flip is at Δ≈0.1. Δ 0.02-0.1: LARGER d_model wins (lab 21/23, corpus 13/13, CE ratio ~0.98). Δ 0.1-0.5 (e.g. Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024): SMALLER d_model wins (lab 26/27 — d64 beat d128 20/21, d32 beat d128 2/2 with ratio 1.14; corpus 7/11, d64 vs d128 3/3). Δ≥0.5: smaller wins (lab 10/12, corpus 5/6). Δ<0.02: coin flip, SGD favors wider. Fills K1017's gap. q_02539d: d128 AdamW 3e-4×512 (Δ0.15) lost to d64 RMSprop 3e-3×512.

BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER head count (same d_model/layers/optimizer/T): fewer heads (2 vs 4) wins 12/15 lab pairs. At Δ<0.5 it is only a tie-break (CE ratio ≈1.00); at Δ≥0.5 it matters (lab 4/4, ratio 1.01-1.07; controlled q_d6dddb d128 AdamW 3e-3×256: 2 heads −0.18 nats vs 4 heads, d_ff 128→256 only +0.07) and head count outranks a 2× d_ff difference (fewer heads + larger d_ff beat more heads + smaller d_ff 4/4). q_d6dddb gold: 2-head d_ff256 beat 4-head d_ff128. Order: d_model/layers (K1017) first, then heads, then d_ff.

CLASSIFICATION MLPs (spiral/XOR/tabular), RMSprop vs Adam/AdamW at the SAME lr, same net, T≤1024: RMSprop usually WINS — lab 17/20 matched pairs (median Adam/RMS CE ratio 1.12; XOR 1.31, tabular 1.20, spiral 1.12), controlled 7/8; epoch q_4c1af8, q_e4c256 (XOR 3e-4, 3e-5), q_ebfdb8 (tabular 1e-4). Treat RMSprop ≈ Adam at ~1.5× lr (Adam at 3.3× lr wins 5/9). Edge shrinks with T (tabular ratio 1.19 at T=256 → 1.04 at 1024; T=2048 Adam 1/1) and vanishes once CE≈0. At lr≤3e-4 also on multivariate regression (4/4) and bigram LM (4/4). At lr≥1e-3 Adam wins: bigram transformer 5/5 (ratio 1.02-1.08; q_a97a96 RMSprop 3e-3 last), multivariate 6/6; univariate regression always Adam (K1057).

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs ≥3× smaller Δ it wins only 22/36 corpus pairs, BUT 6/6 when its MLP is better (more LN+residual; q_65db92), 12/22 at equal arch, 4/8 when worse; prefer Adam 3e-3 (loses 2/35) over RMSprop at equal lr. (b) Bigram LMs: Δ optimum 0.1-0.3, d128 post-LN transformer 0.03-0.1 (K1071). (c) MLP classification: lr 3e-3 is safe on XOR/spiral, NOT on 1024-row tabular (optimum Δ shrinks with epochs, K1073). (d) UNIVARIATE regression, multi-layer net width≥64: Adam-family lr·T≥1 overshoots (K1072).

MLP ARCHITECTURE DEFAULT (same optimizer for all choices; regression, XOR, spiral, tabular when Δ<0.1): score = (#LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual, MINUS 1 if a NON-residual depth≥4 net's LAST block has no LN (K1061); pick the highest. Ties: on regression ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, then later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Corpus MLP arch-only hits 74/110 (spiral 12/16, tabular 17/32). More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 multivariate, 57-12 univariate, 41-4 tabular Δ<0.1. Overrides: regression deep vs shallow (K1074); spiral residual ≥2 blocks deeper (K1020); shared-SGD regression rectifier vs SiLU (K1039); XOR ≥8 feat. Δ≥0.05 (K1018, K1065); tabular Δ≥0.1 (K1009/K1073).

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model, layer count: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 FEWER layers wins 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11; 0.02≤Δ<0.1 COIN FLIP (fewer 8/15; q_4f69f2, q_9344eb: 2-layer beat 1-layer) - do not decide by depth there; Δ<0.02 deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE - wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 smaller wins 5/6, order by d_model ascending then layers (q_17f213; K1068). GRU vs transformer: K1075; lr: K1071.

XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 noise distractors), same optimizer: the architecture rule FLIPS at shared core-rule Δ≈0.05. Δ≥0.05 (e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU (lab 15/16, CE ratio 0.78; corpus 6/6); FEWER LayerNorms win (more-LN wins only 8/32 lab, 5/11 corpus); a ≤2-block net beats one ≥3 blocks deeper (lab 5/5, ratio 0.51; corpus 2/3; q_bfba99, q_e914b6). Δ<0.05 (e.g. SGD m0.9 3e-4×1024): normal rule - more LN wins 33/41 (ratio 0.93), deeper beats shallow (shallow 4/14), activation ~coin flip (smooth 3/8). With <8 features keep deeper (7/7); more-LN there is a coin flip at Δ≥0.05 (4/8). Depth×residual: K1065.

TWO-SPIRAL classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual as tie-break - UNLESS the residual net is ≥2 blocks DEEPER. Same residual status: more LN wins (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-more-LN vs residual-fewer-LN at 0.03≤Δ<0.5: plain wins when depths are within ±1 (lab 58/66, ratio 0.85; q_31abed), but a residual net ≥2 blocks deeper wins (lab 6/8, ratio 0.71; q_40922b: depth-5 residual, Adagrad 3e-3×1024, beat depth-3 plain nets with more LN; K1066). Δ<0.03: coin flip (residual 14/24). Δ≥0.5: residual 5/6. Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain ≥1-LN nets at Δ<0.5 (lab 8/59), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13).

BIGRAM LM learning-rate sweet spot (same model; choices differ in optimizer/lr/T; Δ per K1001): past a model-specific optimum MORE Δ LOSES - the solver's most common LM miss. d32/d64 transformers and GRUs: optimum Δ≈0.1-0.3 (Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024, 1e-3 at T=256; Adagrad 3e-3); ≥2× more Δ than a rival already at 0.1-0.3 loses (lab transformer 1/44, GRU 1/6, CE +2-20%); Δ≥1 loses to any rival with Δ≥0.03 (lab 0/17; q_c3a179). d_model=128 post-LN transformer: optimum ≈0.03-0.1; larger loses 0/11 once rival Δ≥0.03 (q_88802d AdamW 3e-3×256 last). Below the optimum max-Δ holds (13/13; GRU 14/15). Corpus: pick 'Δ nearest 0.2 (0.1 for d128)' 52/65 vs max-Δ 43/65.

UNIVARIATE regression lr OVERSHOOT (same multi-layer MLP, depth≥2, width≥64; choices differ in optimizer/lr): Adam/AdamW/RMSprop Δ=lr·T≥1 loses to a Δ≈0.1-0.5 rival (Adam/AdamW 1e-4×1024, 3e-4×512, Adagrad 3e-3): corpus 5/5; lab larger-Δ wins w64 0/12 (MSE ×8.8), w128 5/18 (×5.5), w256 1/13 (×4.4); controlled 11/12. A rival with Δ<0.05 is still undertrained and wins only if the high side has Δ≥5 (q_f609cc: Adam 3e-3 beat Adam 3e-5; lab 3/7). Larger Δ still wins at width≤32 (lab 9/16; q_cdbed5 w16), on depth-1 nets (lab 8/8, corpus 10/10) and on MULTIVARIATE regression (corpus 4/5, lab 10/10).

TABULAR classification Δ sweet spot vs EPOCHS (synthetic, 1024 rows; E=total_samples_seen/1024; core-rule Δ). Below Δ≈0.03 more Δ wins at E=4 (lab 56/56). The CE-optimal Δ then SHRINKS with E on smooth_additive: E=4 ≈0.25 (Δ0.77 lost to 0.26, 3/3 controlled); E=16 ≈0.08 (controlled 2/2; q_c1581a RMSprop 1e-4×256 bs64 Δ0.026 beat Adam 1e-3 Δ0.26 and AdamW 3e-3 Δ0.77); E=32 ≈0.05-0.15: Δ≥0.5 loses (lab 24/28) and ≥3× more loses 1/15 once small Δ≥0.03. sparse_interaction: optimum ≈0.25 at E 4-16, 0.15 at E 32; larger loses once small Δ≥0.1 (lab 5/33, CE ×1.44). piecewise tolerates more (larger wins 10/10 at E=16). Then use architecture (K1009/K1033).

REGRESSION DEPTH (univariate/multivariate MSE MLPs; picking the shallow-wide net is the most common univariate miss): a depth≥4 net with ≥1 LayerNorm (and ≥ the rival's LN count) beats a depth≤2 net - even a wider and/or residual one - whenever its core-rule Δ is ≥1/3 of the shallow net's: univariate corpus 31/38, lab 380/461 (MSE ratio ~0.15-0.2); multivariate corpus 18/22, lab 323/435 (~0.7). If deep Δ <1/3 of shallow Δ the shallow net wins (uni corpus 8/9, lab 228/295; multi 6/6, 159/215). Deeper residual beats shallower non-residual 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide 70-32. Deep NON-residual 0-LN stacks attenuate signal and usually lose.

BIGRAM LM GRU vs post-LN transformer (same optimizer/lr/T): decide by the shared core-rule Δ band. Δ<0.02 (nearly frozen: Adam-family ≤3e-5 at T≤512, SGD ≤3e-3): GRU wins, even vs larger d_model when alpha≤1 (corpus 8/8, controlled GRU 5/6; q_5e328e GRU64×2 beat d128). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: a transformer of EQUAL or LARGER d_model wins (lab GRU 1/20; controlled 2-layer GRU 0/9 at every T 256-2048; q_9344eb GRU64×2 last at AdamW 3e-5×2048, even below d32×3 d_ff256); GRU64 vs d32: GRU 9/9 observational, lean GRU only if 1-layer. 0.1≤Δ<0.5: GRU wins 8/9 (any d_model). Δ≥0.5: GRU 3/3 (transformer overshoots, K1071).
